archetype.name: Pocket Passer (rhythm distributor)
archetype.definition: A veteran timing thrower who wins from the pocket by getting the ball out on schedule, avoiding sacks and attacking the 10-to-20-yard window, with his legs used for occasional scrambles and goal-line work rather than as a weapon.

report.headline: Elite volume, cleaner pocket than ever; the accuracy is shakier than the box score
report.take:
Dak Prescott is having one of the louder seasons of his career. He is on pace for 4,712 yards and 39 touchdowns, ranks 3rd in passing yards and TDs per game, and sits 9th in EPA per dropback at 0.179. That is a full 0.206 above the qualifier average. The profile is the one he has had for a decade: a 2.81-second time to throw, almost identical to last year's 2.82, a moderate intended air yardage of 8.79, and production built in the intermediate area. His throws of 10-19 air yards are returning 0.378 EPA, and the ones at 20-plus 0.426.

Two things are driving the season. The first is the pocket. He is taking sacks on just 3.4% of dropbacks, 2nd-fewest among qualifiers, and only 15.2% of his pressures become sacks, also 2nd. For a quarterback whose pressure-to-sack rate was 34.8% as recently as 2023, that is a real change. With his time to throw flat, it points at a line that keeps him clean (7th in hit rate allowed) and at him getting rid of the ball under duress. The second driver is script. Dallas owns the league's worst defense by EPA, so he has thrown in a lot of shootouts: 40-46 against San Francisco, 31-34 against Baltimore, 30-33 against Arizona. He has also logged 112 dropbacks trailing by nine or more. The volume is partly a product of what the other side of the ball allows.

The numbers hide some looseness. His bad-throw rate is 15%, 29th of 45 and up 3.8 points from last year's career-best 11.2%. His yards per attempt and completion rate are both slightly down from 2025. Throws to the middle have produced a -3.6 CPOE and three interceptions, and the intermediate window that makes him dangerous also holds four of his six picks. Third down has been flat at 0.004 EPA. The early-season wobble was real: back-to-back losses to Tampa Bay (3rd-ranked defense now) and Green Bay produced negative EPA and most of his interceptions.

Since then he has been very good. Over the last three games he is at 0.312 EPA per dropback and 9.7 adjusted net yards per dropback, with 11 TDs against one pick. The caveat is that this window includes Tennessee (30th defense) and a track meet with the 49ers, and a 9.3% TD rate is not a level anyone holds. The true talent sits between the early dip and this heater: a top-10 efficiency passer whose counting stats will stay near the top of the league as long as Dallas' defense keeps forcing him to throw.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance at a career-best level
strengths.body: He is converting pressure into sacks at a far lower rate than at any point in his charted career. With a near-identical time to throw, the gain comes from the ball coming out and from a line that rarely lets him get hit. It is the most important reason his efficiency holds up on drives that stall elsewhere. Some regression is likely given his history, and especially with a starting guard out.

strengths.title: Intermediate and deep efficiency
strengths.body: Throws of 10-plus air yards are where his value lives, at 0.394 EPA per attempt. George Pickens (0.346 EPA per target) and Ryan Flournoy have turned the outside into a reliable middle-depth game next to CeeDee Lamb's volume. This is his career-long strength, so it should last, with the interception risk that comes attached.

strengths.title: Hot stretch with turnover control
strengths.body: Across his last five games he has one interception, and the last three produced 0.312 EPA per dropback. The ball security is consistent with his recent seasons. The touchdown rate in this stretch is the part that will cool.

concerns.title: Accuracy has slipped from last year
concerns.body: His bad-throw rate has jumped back to his 2018/2024 range after two clean years. His completion rate and yards per attempt are both a touch below 2025. The efficiency is being carried by big plays and sack avoidance more than by ball placement. That makes him more matchup-dependent than his EPA rank suggests.

concerns.title: Middle-of-field and third-down leaks
concerns.body: Throws over the middle carry a negative CPOE and three interceptions. Third down, where he takes many of his sacks, is roughly break-even. These are the plays that decided the Tampa Bay and Green Bay losses, and they are why the floor is lower than the season averages imply. The sample is modest, but it fits the intermediate interception count.

concerns.title: Volume leans on a broken defense
concerns.body: Dallas ranks last in defensive EPA, which has pushed him into shootouts and catch-up passing. That is good for his counting stats. It also means part of the yardage comes in game states where defenses concede underneath. If the script flips to comfortable leads, attempts drop.

trend.note: After a two-game trough against Tampa Bay and Green Bay with negative EPA and four combined picks, he has been positive every week since. The last three games are his best stretch of the year. Some of that comes against soft defenses, and the bad-throw rate hasn't improved with it.

nextGame.headline: Thanksgiving rematch with a beatable, banged-up Eagles secondary
nextGame.body:
Philadelphia's pass defense ranks 24th in EPA and is 31st in hit rate, so the clean-pocket game that defines his season should hold. He already carved this defense in Week 7, throwing three touchdowns on 27 attempts with his most aggressive downfield profile of the season. WR1s have scored above their averages against the Eagles and posted 0.42 EPA per target (25th), which sets up Lamb. The resistance comes at tight end, where Philadelphia has held TE1s under their norms, but Jake Ferguson is out anyway.

Availability tilts his way on the other side: top corner Quinyon Mitchell (92% of snaps) left last game with a hamstring and is questionable on a short week, and linebacker Zack Baun is on IR, which softens the middle where Prescott has been loosest. On his side, guard Tyler Booker (94% of snaps) is out, a real test for the interior protection behind his sack numbers. Ferguson and Mingo being out narrows the target tree further toward Lamb, Pickens and Flournoy. The main cap is script. Dallas is an 8.5-point favorite against a 29th-ranked offense whose QB Tanner McKee is nursing ribs, and the 47.5 total is far below the totals of his recent shootouts. A comfortable lead could mean fewer second-half attempts.

keyMatchups.title: Lamb against a soft WR1 defense
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles have allowed 0.42 EPA per target to opposing WR1s, among the worst marks in the league. If Mitchell can't go, Lamb's volume role gets an easier draw. This is the clearest path to a big yardage day.

keyMatchups.title: Interior protection without Booker
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia barely gets home, ranking 31st in hit rate and 23rd in sack rate. That should cushion the loss of a starting guard. If the interior holds, he gets the clean pockets he had in Week 7.

keyMatchups.title: Lead-protecting game script
keyMatchups.body: With Dallas a heavy favorite and the Eagles' offense struggling, a multi-score lead is plausible. He has been very efficient when up big. That efficiency comes on few attempts, which trims his ceiling more than his floor.

nextGame.watch: Whether Quinyon Mitchell plays: without him, the intermediate outside throws to Lamb and Pickens should be open all day.

restOfSeason.body:
The foundation is sustainable: an unchanged time to throw, a clean pocket, and a receiver group producing well above average per target. All of that should keep him a top-10 efficiency passer and top-five in volume. Dallas' defense is unlikely to fix itself, so passing volume stays high. The last three games' touchdown rate and 0.312 EPA per dropback will come down. Expect something closer to 260-295 yards and roughly two touchdowns a game, with interceptions creeping back toward his career norm given the elevated bad-throw rate.

The sack rate is the number most likely to regress, especially with Booker out into December. A few extra sacks would nudge his efficiency toward the season mark rather than the recent one. The rushing contribution is minor and mostly scrambles and goal-line sneaks.
swingFactors: Dallas' defense forcing shootouts or not
Interior protection while Booker is out
Whether the bad-throw rate tightens or produces more intermediate picks

confidence.note: 11 healthy starts, a stable role and a profile consistent with his career; the touchdown rate is the main noise.
